sentences.text:
Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao
Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao
 Criminal Petition No.6138 Of 2019
Order:

1. In this Criminal Petition, filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., the petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2 seek to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.75 of 2019 of Koilakuntla Police Station,
Kurnool district, which was registered against them for the offences under Sections 188 and 273 of IPC and Sections 58 and 59(i) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the FSS Act').

2. The allegations against the petitioners/accused Nos.1 and 2, briefly, are that on 13.05.2019 at 11:30 hours, when the complainant along with his staff, as no mediators came forward to act as panchayatdars, rushed to buddy shop of A-1, found him selling the banned tobacco products therein,
having purchased the same from the petitioner/accused No.2, owner of Andhra Medical Shop,
Koilakuntla, and on interrogation as the accused voluntarily confessed to have been engaged in the business of prohibited tobacco products, seized the same, registered F.I.R. and remanded him to judicial custody for the offences stated supra.
3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He UDPR,J relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto on the report of the Sub-Inspector of Police, Koilakuntla Police Station, Kurnool district.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as Section 188 of IPC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.
